entries.note: Full text (PMC3470466). Quote verbatim, truncated first clause; 'not predicted from pathway models' also verbatim. Stated in-vitro gene-set vs lesional-biopsy comparison supports same. Only gap: no untested opener (rule 6).

PharmR BLA 125504 (signed B. Hill 2014-08-07) section 1.2, verbatim. Cyno studies are numbered 070204-03/0770712-01 (2007) and FIH RA dosing began 2005-12 (NCT00669942), so first use predates 2009; 2009 is only the earliest date the review cites.

Quote verbatim (section 1.2). A NOAEL margin is a toxicology ceiling, not an exposure/occupancy target; no cyno-derived efficacy exposure or IL-17A occupancy was compared with patients. Belongs in safety (immunotoxicity prediction held). Dose stays untested; entry becomes redundant.

Abstract verbatim. Acceptable model-exists opener, but not the class's relied-on model: FDA review filed no psoriasis efficacy model (only in-vitro neutralization, cyno tox, three infection models). Rizzo 2011 DOI verified (epub 2010-12-20, IL-23-injection model, blocking anti-IL-17A).

Abstract verbatim (PMID 20926833). CIA/EAE/EAU appear only as background; no psoriasis-model-vs-PASI comparison is made, and a human POC is not a preclinical model. Under the context rule this is untested (or drop: no status change). registry_date 2015-04-10 = NCT00669916 confirmed.

Abstract verbatim; Conti 2009 DOI verified (IL-17RA-/- mice severe OPC). Neither is the relied-on model (filed = cynomolgus tox, 2007-2009 study numbers). Possible earlier opener Ogawa 2004 anti-IL-17 DSS colitis, unverified (see missing).

Quote verbatim (Discussion). Model fails relied-on rule: filed cyno tox mentions no bowel/colitis/intestine; IBD exacerbations in PsO trials (label 5.4; Candida 1.2 vs 0.3%) mean its silence failed, so contra, 2015 (label/review). Candida half cites human CMC genetics, not mouse.

missing: safety: the relied-on, filed models are absent. 26-week cynomolgus tox (PharmR BLA 125504 sections 1.2/6.2; zero mentions of bowel, colitis, intestine or Crohn's) should open the strip (2009 or earlier, untested) and carry the contra; the filed mouse OPC special-tox study (PharmR section 10, Novartis study 1270309: 'anti-IL-17A-treated mice failing to clear infection by Day 4') matched label Candida 1.2% vs 0.3% - a filed same for Candida that contra overrides.

safety: Ogawa 2004, Clin Immunol 110:55-62 (neutralising anti-IL-17 aggravated DSS colitis in mice) would open the colitis-model strip in 2004 with a class-proxy antibody; the Gut paper's 'T cell independent models of colitis' points at it. Not verified this session (budget) - check DOI before use.

efficacy: Krueger 2012 full text states 'Studies in mouse model systems indicate that IL-22 is required for the psoriasis phenotype' and that rapid attenuation of epidermal hyperplasia 'was not predicted'. If the IL-23-injection mouse model (Zheng 2007) is treated as a psoriasis model used for the class, this is a published mouse under-prediction (scaling, possibly contra) for efficacy in 2012. Not pursued.

dose: nothing found - no cynomolgus-derived efficacy exposure or occupancy target was ever published against patient PK/PD; the human POC (Hueber 2010, 3-10 mg/kg iv) set the exposure. This confirms untested rather than adds an entry.

registry: ERASURE NCT01365455 results first posted 2015-05-29 (CAIN457A2302), core Crohn's trial NCT00584740 2015-03-31 (CAIN457A2202), extension NCT01009281 2021-07-12 - all three draft dates confirmed against the CT.gov v2 API.
rule_questions: Cross-indication comparisons: when the only published model-vs-patient comparison sits in another disease (Crohn's patients for safety; CIA/EAE/EAU models for efficacy), does it score in this context? The brief's `other` key covers other mechanism only; there is no key for other disease. I applied a strict psoriasis-population reading: efficacy untested; safety contra dated to the PsO label (2015) rather than to Hueber 2012.

Relied-on model vs literature model: a never-filed literature model (IL-17A-deficient transfer colitis) flagged a harm the filed cynomolgus tox missed, and the sponsor's own trial title calls the outcome 'unexpected'. The brief's 'best model = relied on' plus 'silence' wording gives contra on the filed model; the drafter scored the literature model same. Confirm contra is intended when a published model got it right but the class did not use it - that mismatch is the finding.

Exposure margin as a dose comparison: the FDA sentence 'Clinical dosing at 1/10th the NOAEL (300 mg/60 kg = 5 mg/kg) did not significantly decrease total lymphocytes' is verbatim and the source itself makes the comparison, but a NOAEL is a safety ceiling, not an exposure/occupancy target. I scored dose untested; if margin statements are meant to count as dose `same`, many antibody contexts will flip and the brief should say so.

Human proof-of-concept in the model field: the atlas is of preclinical models; a human POC trial should not be a `model`. If the class genuinely skipped animal models for a question, the cell should stay untested on whatever model existed (IMQ / IL-23-injection mouse) with the POC in the note.

Contra by juxtaposition: contra on the filed cyno tox rests on FDA-review silence plus the label's IBD warning (comparison_stated false). Rule 1 asks for a source that makes the comparison; the house example ad-amyloid (Egan 2019) is the same shape, so I assumed juxtaposition is acceptable for silence-contra. Confirm.
Rule 6 opener: engagement starts at same 2012 with no untested entry because model first use equals the comparison year; acceptable, or should an opener be synthesised?
